scope: Source and fresh 29/0 material assignment/lifecycle evidence after one targeted lifetime correction; no GPU rendering
findings: Cloth next_pass injects the exact primary GPU_VERTEX hook and copies all eight deformation parameters, including render offset.
Only the shader is static; each source material owns its pass and actor textures through material metadata. No Node or actor state is stored in a global cache.
CreatureBall keeps native surfaces on the existing shared owner rim and changes only the cloth material selected by its active gpu_driven contract.
Owner changes and pooled reparent retain the same per-cape material while preserving other actors' uniforms.

ModelLifetime detaches the retained pass, disables gpu_driven and clears texture references before freeing the model. It now retains the detached ShaderMaterial itself until the same frame boundary as the base material. A WeakRef with no external strong pass reference proves live-after-release and freed-after-frame behavior. Vendor teardown separately invalidates its shared Texture2DRD wrappers.
The unchanged vendor solver and preparation cache hashes do not require new canonical cache compatibility exceptions.

The test uses synthetic ShaderMaterial textures and a real CreatureBall assignment/ModelLifetime release path; its 29 assertions do not establish shader compilation, cloth simulation or rendered rim alignment.
resolved_followup: Removing next_pass and metadata initially dropped the last pass reference too early. clear_rim now returns that pass and ModelLifetime includes it in held; the targeted WeakRef assertions cover the previously masked lifetime gap.
required_remaining_acceptance: Physical GPU with current ordinary CreatureBall/SCN, real cape solver, both owner colors, idle/attack and rear/side captures; hardware renderer label and source hashes.
